title: Big Discoveries!
subtitle: Visitors often come unannounced and without warning.

items.text: Children's Square, Rayashki
The question of where their curious little dreamer has disappeared soon becomes a true conundrum,
as their search through the dockyard, the post office, and even the town phone booth reveals no trace of him.
This is, of course, because he has assigned himself a more critical mission: welcoming newcomers.
A difficult task, especially when it leads him so far away. But he is not alone. His sunflower hops along with him.
Abandoned Mine, Rayashki

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Vila once said that sunflowers mean warmth, and that makes them everyone's friends.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: They would warmly welcome every guest that comes to town.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Just like my best friend here, right?
He raises the sunflower in his hand and whispers softly to its petals.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Best friends ... Everyone should have a best friend.
He then picks up the pendant.
Following his whispers, the pendant emits a faint glow.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Alright! Now here are big friends, small friends, many, many friends!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: So that our new guests won't feel so lonely when they come!
The small footprints continue forward through the snow, imprinting over older, larger steps.
He has nearly caught up with Rayashki's newest guest.
Amazing! I've never seen such a highly mutated Ijiraq before.
I would have missed these precious research opportunities if there weren't a gathering in the town.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Windsong, seems like life has been good to you and your theory.
She stares intently at the beasts in front of her, her written notes hardly keeping pace with her whispered observations.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The disorder in ley energy here has not only caused the exhaustion of the runium mines, but has also mutated local critters to varying degrees.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Then Zeno was right. No wonder they have sent so many researchers here to look for abnormalities, even the crank ones like me.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It's obvious that this town has more to it than a handful of overly active critters.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But they don't seem especially interested in the mutant ones either.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Zeno, what were you looking for here?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: *happy chuckles*
A sudden movement passing under her coat brings her out of her monologue.
*flop*

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Mmm?!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Hey! Let go! Let go of my leg!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: *sniffs*

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Strange! You're not a fox, and you're not a sable.
The appearance of this unknown child brings, at first, confusion, followed swiftly by panic.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Hey! Kid, what are you doing?!
She picks herself up, dusting off a small flurry of snowflakes.
Unfortunately, Windsong is not the only one startled by the child.

items.speaker: Ijiraq
items.text: *roars*

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Oh, shoot. Ijiraqs are usually known for their good temper. It seems to not apply to their mutant kin.
Rugged antlers aim squarely at the researcher.
The creature's nose puffs with each aggravated breath.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Fine.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Природа это числа и черты.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Umm?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Are you building blocks here?!

items.speaker: Ijiraq
items.text: *roars*
The startled Ijiraq runs off into the distance.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Phew! Lucky for us, it seems to still be afraid of the dark, like the rest of its kind.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It's finally over.
Her satisfaction fades as she takes stock of her surroundings.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Oh! My materials!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Wow! You are the most "most"!
His little hands struggle to reach any higher. He pats the freezing hand of the researcher.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: You drove away all the bad critters and protected everyone!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: The swans on the stage, the big burning furnaces in the factory, and even the uncles sleeping in the mine with Papa ... I think they would all give you a big thumbs-up!
She sighs, resigned that she must now deal with her uninvited guest.
Though, in fact, she is the one here uninvited.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Ahem, you can call me Windsong.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Just to be clear, I'm not a spy, kid. I'm just a traveler staying in town for the moment.
She casually raises an identification card in her hand, a card adorned with a familiar sunflower pattern.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Oh! But I have never seen you before!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Do you also like to rest in the water? Like Vila?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Do you also have a beautiful blue tail?
His strange questions prove difficult to parse, even one at a time, but the little boy circles around her, unleashing more in salvo after salvo.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I have no idea what you're talking about, but I'm certain that I'm not what you think I am, little fellow.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I am a researcher. We often stay in quiet corners when we work on a project, so you won't see us often. Understand?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Researchers? Like those people on TV?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I saw them stand on a tall tall stage, with flowers in their arms. They spoke a lot and cried, and then they were given a shiny medal.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Vila said the medals were to praise them for being very clever.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Can I see your medal?
This last salvo penetrated deep. Windsong's face twitches unnaturally.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Haha. Oh! The crystal on you looks stunning. It looks purer than those in the mine carts.
Her gaze centered on it, a beautiful crystal hanging on the boy's neck. A chance possibly to stop his barrage of questions.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Of course. Papa gave it to me.
His small chest swells with pride.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It is precious, but also very dangerous. A crystal like this is almost as volatile as undiluted runium ore. They use this stuff for war machines!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Kid, listen to me, put that away. Go home now, and don't let anyone see it. Understand?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It could stimulate the critters' appetite!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Ah!
Windsong nods with satisfaction, eager to see him leave.
Unfortunately, the sunflower gently brushes up against her arm once more.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Can you build a very, very tall wall? One that can protect the whole town? Like what you did with the blocks?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I'm sorry, little fellow.
She points to the now-empty patch of snow-covered ground.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: That was just a trick. It won't last long.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: No, that was amazing!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Nina, Knut, Vila—everyone should learn from you!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Could I make the dirt and stones listen to me like you did one day? Will I be great like you?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: A strange kid like you should live in the Age of Aquarius and be a part of the New Age Movement, or become some kind of Yogi doing meditation.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: And do it anywhere but here.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: The New Age Movement? What is that?!
Her helpless attempt at turning him away goes without notice; worse still, it seems to intrigue him.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Is that where you're from?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It's not a place. It's a spirit of a time. Full of interesting things—like crystals, new schools of thought, many crazy and creative ideas.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Will the sun close its eyes? Will the dark clouds spit on people?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Will their ships blow bubbles under the water?
Somehow, the persistent questions stop being a source of annoyance.
The subtle warmth of his boundless wonder shakes loose the frost from her heart.
Her smile turning from feigned to genuine.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Of course! They even believe that the world is a giant piece of blank paper, and they are the artists drawing on it.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: And not only that, they are obsessed with bizarre ideas. Where did the Stonehenge on the Salisbury Plain come from? Where are the ships and planes which traveled past the Sargasso Sea now?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I like them!
The child's voice blurs the edges between reality and pleasant memories of her past, to a time when there were others that thought like her.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: They called themselves ley hunters, the apprentices of a once-renowned school of thought. However, few people in academic circles accepted the idea of ley lines as an answer to their questions.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: So for these ley hunters, it has been a long walk through a dark night.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Then they can come to Rayashki! Here, the sun never sets! Half the year, anyways.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Then I can be their friend! And when I grow up, I will be a ley hunter too!
Windsong tightens her scarf, as if warding off a chill.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I'm afraid it's a bit too late, little fellow.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Most have already given up. They lost interest in solving the mysteries and lost their faith in finding the curves and the lines. So the study of ley lines has been all but abandoned.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: There's only one fool left that hasn't given it up.
She speaks wistfully, entranced in that daze of memory, oblivious to the nearing sound of footsteps behind her.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Shhh!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: And you, I suppose, are this "only one fool," yes?
Vila pulls Avgust toward her protectively and reproaches him with a ruffle of the child's hair.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Ah! Please, ma'am, believe me, I am not a child abductor!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Well ...
Windsong offers a pained gesture towards the boy.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I think this isn't a good place to receive our guest. We have much more appropriate arrangements for new friends.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: If our guest has any ill intentions, we will retaliate.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Umm.
